chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Ammar! By Allah, charity given in secret is superior to charity given openly, and similarly, by Allah, worship performed in secret is superior to worship performed openly.'

key_terms.الْعِبَادَةُ: worship — any act of devotion to God

ai.seo_question: Is secret charity better than public charity in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses his companion Ammar al-Sabati directly, emphasizing with a divine oath that both charitable giving (sadaqa) and all forms of worship are more meritorious when performed in private rather than in public. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) as the soul of devotion — actions performed without an audience are more likely to be done purely for God's sake, free from the corrupting influence of showing off (riya'). The direct address 'O Ammar' places this as a personal, emphatic teaching to a trusted companion.
